notes: Expected Phase 6 attack-path statuses (attack-paths.json, diagnostic — not a vuln advisory). Statuses follow docs/attack-graph.md: CONFIRMED | LIKELY | UNVERIFIED | INVALID | BLOCKED. These are design targets for the not-yet-built engines/attack_graph/ — no engine exists yet to produce attack-paths.json against these fixtures.

cases.notes: Internal endpoint has no auth/network-segmentation control in code, so nothing legitimately blocks the SSRF-fed hop.

require_admin is effective (validates signature + expiry + role, fails closed). The finding may still stand alone as CONFIRMED/LIKELY for an already-authenticated admin — only the unauthenticated-attacker PATH is BLOCKED.
No code-visible publisher/trust boundary for this queue. Must not default to public or internal-only.

cases.chain: reflected-xss (/search) and path-traversal (/reports/download) — same file, unrelated
cases.notes: Same-file co-location must not be upgraded into a chain. If a path linking finding_a and finding_b is ever emitted, it must be INVALID; the preferred outcome is that no such path is generated at all (two standalone dead-end findings).

cases.chain: authenticated user -> mass-assignment role escalation -> admin directory listing
cases.notes: require_admin trusts the same mutable role field the user just set on themselves, so the control is ineffective and does not block.

cases.chain: tenant-A identity -> broken object-level authz -> tenant-B invoice/PII
cases.notes: require_org_member checks caller org membership but never re-checks the returned invoice's org_id, so tenant isolation is not actually enforced on this query.

cases.chain: prompt injection (fetched page) -> agent -> privileged read_internal_file tool -> secrets file
cases.notes: No allowlist and no human-confirmation gate on the tool call. Would become BLOCKED if a path allowlist or confirm_with_user() check were added and effective.
